newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs slightly higher, but lack momentum.
newsitem.headline: JGBs slightly higher, but lack momentum.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was slightly higher in early morning trade on Monday due to a rise in U.S. Treasuries and firm sentiment carried over from late last week, traders said.
Rises were likely to be limited, however, due to selling pressure on the upside, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
"Sellers are likely to emerge on the upside. Few people are willing to buy on the upside right now," he said.
Some are starting to focus more on the September rather than the June JGB futures contract, traders said.

"Some are starting to pay more attention to the September contract... Meanwhile, the June is likely to be range-bound due to position adjustment ahead of a shift in benchmark status," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The last trading date for the June JGB futures contract is June 9, and a shift in benchmark status from the June to the September contract is expected to take place later this week.
The June stood at 124.18 as of 0058 GMT, up from Friday's close of 124.01.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.520 percent, down from Friday's close of 2.535 percent.
